title: IAM policy templates and environment scoping guidance
content:
Purpose:
This working draft collects practical IAM role templates, environment scoping rules, and operational guidance for automating evidence collection and SIEM export mappings. The goal is to provide ready-to-copy policy fragments and concrete scoping choices for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments so teams can enforce least privilege consistently while retaining traceable audit evidence.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: platform/security engineers, solutions engineering, SREs who onboard customers, and compliance reviewers.
- Scope: RBAC-style role templates (coarse-grained roles + policy slices), environment-specific constraints, audit log field mapping, and an evidence automation checklist (scripts + schedules).

Design principles (short):
- Least privilege by default: role templates are deliberately narrow; compose where necessary.
- Environment scoping: treat Hosted, Dedicated, and Private as different trust zones with graduated privileges and access patterns.
- Observable by design: every template includes minimum audit logging expectations (who/what/when/ctx).
- Automatable evidence: prefer machine-consumable outputs for audits (JSON snapshots, signed timestamps).

Environment scoping overview:
1) Hosted (multi-tenant control plane + managed compute):
   - Only Redwood control plane employees and select on-call SREs have console-level elevated roles.
   - Customer tenants get API keys and scoped service roles (no access to other tenants).
   - Access via RBAC: role bindings must include tenant_id and route filters; use attribute-based conditions for admin actions.

2) Dedicated (single-tenant reserved capacity):
   - Customer-managed workspace with Redwood operator support.
   - Operators get time-bound support sessions via jump roles; all support access requires Just-In-Time (JIT) approval and session recording.
   - Service accounts used by infra for autoscaling must be scoped to GPU pools; no cross-customer resource access.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem):
   - Control plane may be customer-hosted; Redwood support acts as a remote consultant with no direct root access unless explicitly contracted.
   - Where Redwood runs a thin agent, the agent principal is scoped to telemetry and update endpoints only.

Suggested high-level role matrix (conceptual):
- Viewer: read-only visibility for metrics, logs, and billing; no configuration changes.
- Operator: can change infra-level configs (scale, patch), but not customer data or secrets.
- Admin: wide config and deployment control; used sparingly and subject to approval.
- Support-JIT: temporary elevated rights with session recording and expiration.
- Customer-Service: tenant-scoped API key with limited endpoints (generate-embedding, generate-text but not model-management).

Policy template snippets (JSON-like, adapt to cloud provider or internal policy language):

1) Tenant-scoped API key role (minimal):
{
  "role": "tenant_api_user",
  "description": "API key for customer app integration - cannot modify models or billing",
  "permissions": [
    "inference.generate", 
    "inference.stream", 
    "usage.read"
  ],
  "conditions": {
    "tenant_id": "${TENANT_ID}",
    "caller_ip": "${ALLOWED_IPS} || null",
    "time_restriction": "optional"
  }
}

Notes: require token rotation policy and restrict issuance to registered service accounts. For hosted, tie token issuance to tenant onboarding flow.

2) Operator role for Dedicated (requires JIT):
{
  "role": "dedicated_operator",
  "description": "Manage dedicated capacity pools - requires active JIT session",
  "permissions": [
    "capacity.scale",
    "pool.update",
    "monitoring.read",
    "logs.read"
  ],
  "conditions": {
    "jitauth": true,
    "session_id": "non-null",
    "session_recording": "enabled"
  }
}

3) Private deploy agent principal (very narrow):
{
  "role": "private_agent",
  "description": "Thin agent for telemetry and updates on private installs",
  "permissions": [
    "telemetry.write",
    "updates.check",
    "config.read_lite"
  ],
  "conditions": {
    "allowed_endpoints": ["agent.redwood.net", "updates.redwood.net"],
    "tls_mutual_auth": true
  }
}

Audit log schema (minimum fields to emit):
- timestamp: ISO8601
- event_id: stable UUID
- actor: principal id (user/serviceaccount)
- actor_type: user | service | agent
- tenant_id: optional tenant identifier
- action: canonical action string (e.g., inference.generate, iam.grant)
- resource: canonical resource id (model:abc123, pool:eu-west-1-a)
- resource_type: model | pool | config | secret
- outcome: success | denied | error
- request_attrs: JSON blob with request shape metadata (token_count, model_variant, seq_len)
- trace_id: correlated trace for request path
- policy_snapshot: id or hash of policy version that was evaluated

SIEM export mapping (recommended fields + notes):
- Elastic index name: redwood-audit-%{+YYYY.MM.dd}
- Mapping:
  timestamp -> @timestamp
  event_id -> event.id
  actor -> user.name or process.name
  action -> event.action
  resource -> file.path or cloud.resource.id
  outcome -> event.outcome
  request_attrs -> event.metadata.request
  trace_id -> trace.id

Transport options: JSON-over-HTTPS (preferred) with mutual TLS and per-customer API tokens for Dedicated exports. For Hosted, export is push-only from internal exporters; do not expose internal keys. Provide configurable filtering by tenant_id to avoid cross-tenant leaks.

Evidence automation checklist (for audits, quarterly):
1) IAM snapshot export (monthly): export all role bindings, service accounts, and policies to signed JSON (include hash).
   - Command example: redwood-iam export --format json --sign --out /evidence/iam-snapshot-2024-11.json
2) Access review report (quarterly): list of principals with Admin or Operator roles, their last activity, and approval ticket link.
3) Support session records (per-session): store session recording URL, session_id, initiator, approver, and timestamps.
4) Config drift snapshot for Dedicated/Private (daily): capture pool configs, autoscale policies, and kernel choices.
5) Audit log retention manifest (monthly): signed manifest of retained indices and S3/Blob URIs.

Automation implementation notes:
- Prefer server-side generation of evidence artifacts with immutable storage (S3 with Object Lock or equivalent) to prevent tampering.
- Sign every artifact with an Org-level key and store signature metadata in the evidence index of the SIEM.
- Use short-lived interior tokens for the automation runner and rotate keys monthly.

Quick-run script pseudocode (concept):
- run_evidence_cycle.sh:
  1) export_iam_snapshot -> iam.json
  2) sign iam.json -> iam.json.sig
  3) upload iam.json and sig to s3://redwood-evidence/YYYY/MM/
  4) post manifest to /evidence-manifests (immutable)
  5) push a manifest event to SIEM ingestion endpoint

Operational guardrails and approval flows:
- Any role grant that yields Admin or Operator must have a linked approval ticket and an expiration date. Automated checks should reject bind requests without these fields.
- JIT sessions must be created via the central approval service and create a one-time session token that contains the approval_id.

Appendix: quick references and example Jira/Confluence links:
- Confluence policy catalog: CONFLUENCE-1234
- SIEM export config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/456
- JIRA tickets used in templates: JIRA-SC-78, JIRA-SC-102

Open questions to resolve (for next revision):
- How granular should tenant-scoped condition language be for hosted keys (IP + CIDR + app-id)?
- Default rotation cadence for Dedicated support keys vs. Hosted customer keys?
- Do we require hardware-backed signing (HSM) for quarterly evidence finalization?

Owner & reviewers:
- Owner: Priya Natarajan (security-compliance)
- Reviewers: Ethan Morales, Li Zhang, Marta Rivera

Status notes: draft templates and mappings in this doc are intended to be converted into enforcement policies in the policy engine and into a SIEM ingest template. Reviewers: please mark inline comments and point to existing infra PRs when you propose changes.
